plans.summary:
Cause and ownership: Controls combines configuration with frequently used Skill and Site actions. Strengthen the existing navigation structure: the shell owns consistent dropdown layout and interaction; settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js retain ownership of their lists, creation flows, and execution. No new domain concept or backend capability is needed. Reviewed runtime intent under /home/buddy/projects/refine/docs/intent and current worktree source. Substantial matching edits and a new navigation test already exist; preserve and complete them. No repository files were changed during planning, and tests were not run.

Task #1 - Review the existing diff against this Round before editing. Retain applicable work and preserve unrelated changes; treat existing implementation and tests as unverified.

Task #2 - Complete the shell structure in index.html: right-align Skills, Sites, Settings, and + New Goal in that order. Move the existing Skill and Site sections into their respective dropdowns and rename visible Controls references, accessible labels, and contextual help to Settings. Preserve existing configuration routes, Node and Reporter selectors, status controls, and related New Goal actions.

Task #3 - Complete the menus through their existing feature owners. Skills lists applicable enabled Custom Skills, followed by one separator and New Skill / Manage Skills. Sites lists Knowledge Hub sites, followed by one separator and New Site / Manage Sites. Reuse existing creation modals; management links target #/settings/skills and #/settings/knowledge-hub. Preserve Skill input preflight and agent-tab launch, plus published and draft Site opening behavior. Keep creation and management accessible for empty or failed lists.

Task #4 - Complete shared interaction and styling in common.js and base.css. Reuse existing dropdown summaries, icons, rows, spacing, colors, and focus treatment. Ensure mutual exclusion, outside-click and Escape dismissal, and closing after actions. Refresh through existing feature and node-context mechanisms on opening and relevant changes; discard stale responses. Verify panels remain reachable and scrollable on narrow screens and with long lists.

Task #5 - Align navigation, Skills, and Knowledge Hub intent documentation and affected Guide/onboarding text with the final menu locations. Describe Sites as the navigation entry to the existing Knowledge Hub capability.

Task #6 - Verify the completed behavior with the existing static navigation contract and browser suites: web_topbar_navigation, web_controls_node_selector, web_knowledge_hub, and web_screen_render. Cover exact order and exclusive placement, separators, both creation and management flows, Skill launch, draft and published Site links, empty/error states, refresh races, keyboard interaction, and preserved Settings controls. Inspect desktop and narrow layouts with long names/lists in both themes. Run browser checks with working Chromium; report skips as unverified. Run git diff --check and distinguish unrelated baseline failures from regressions.

skill.prompt:
## Implementation

Implement the current Goal Round using all accepted plans and attached Skills. Inspect existing code, make the complete change, run appropriate verification, and report evidence for each checklist item. Check the plan's assumptions against the code and keep policy in its shared owner. Prefer one correction that explains the affected behavior over separate fixes at each failing call site. Report evidence-backed plan deviations within the Goal's scope and existing authority. Preserve unrelated changes and historical evidence.

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

### Semantic code organization

Keep each code file focused on one cohesive responsibility. Treat roughly 500 lines as a prompt to review structure, not as a blind hard cap. When a file grows because it mixes responsibilities or unrelated method families, split it into clearly named modules or files and move methods, helpers, types, and tests with the responsibility they serve. Prefer real module boundaries and stable public APIs over arbitrary chunks or include-only shards. Preserve behavior during structural refactors, and document any justified exception for generated or intrinsically cohesive files.

If issues outside the Goal’s scope block progress, investigate and fix them or use an evidence-backed workaround, preserving required checks and documenting what you changed.
